turns.prompt_text: I'm using Notion. I'm pretty new to it. I'm looking at some different YouTube videos for people using it to help with their ADHD. I have a board up with kind of a Trello-like flow to it. It's an Agile board. I have three sprints on one day this week, for morning, evening, and night each one is three hours. I may not use; I probably won't use all three sprints. But I would like these three sprints to reoccur every week on Tuesday.
turns.response_html:
Setting up recurring sprints in Notion is a great way to reduce the "decision fatigue" that often comes with ADHD. Since you want these to repeat every Tuesday, the best way to handle this is using Database Automations or Recurring Templates.

Here is the most efficient way to set this up so your morning, evening, and night sprints pop up automatically:

1. Create a Recurring Template

Instead of manually copying your sprints, you can tell Notion to "spawn" them for you.

  1. Open your Agile database.
  2. Click the arrow next to the blue New button in the top right and select + New template.
  3. Title it "Morning Sprint" (and add any properties like "3 Hours" or "Morning" tag).
  4. Go back to that arrow menu. You'll see "Morning Sprint" in the list.
  5. Click the three dots (...) next to the template name and select Repeat.
  6. Set it to Weekly, every Tuesday, and pick a time (e.g., 6:00 AM).
  7. Repeat this process for "Evening Sprint" and "Night Sprint."

2. Managing the "I Might Not Use It" Aspect

Since you mentioned you probably won't use all three, you want to avoid "digital clutter" where unused sprints just sit there looking like failed tasks.

  • The "Draft" Status: Add a status called "Planned" or "Tentative" to your board. Have the templates auto-populate with this status. If the time passes and you don't move it to "In Progress," you can simply delete it or have a filter that hides "Planned" tasks from previous days.
  • The "One-Click" Alternative: If you find the automatic pop-up distracting, don't set a "Repeat" schedule. Just keep the Templates. When Tuesday rolls around, you can click the template name, and it instantly creates that 3-hour block only when you're actually ready to commit.

3. ADHD Optimization Tips

  • Visual Cues: Use different icons for each (e.g., 🌅 for Morning, 🌙 for Night). It makes the board easier to "scan" at a glance.
  • The "Brain Dump" Area: Since you're using an Agile flow, make sure you have a "Backlog" column. When a sprint starts, only drag in what you really think you can do in those 3 hours.

Would you like me to find a specific Notion formula that can automatically calculate if you're over-booking those 3-hour blocks?
